items.text: Hello, Tacticians,
This is Jinsang Kim, Creative Director of Lost Eidolons: Veil of the Witch.
How did you enjoy the winter update of 2025?

That update focused primarily on reducing the fatigue of repeated playthroughs by increasing build variety and overall gameplay variety, based on the feedback many of you shared. We added Blessed Relics (enhanced versions of relics), introduced new passive skills for each character, and implemented the Morale Boost system to help Tacticians discover new team combinations by encouraging the use of less-played characters.
For the upcoming February update, we are preparing three major features as outlined below.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/6ae03e99a8f32984cc8e9af8c5ec582f93877a1e.png"]With this update, we are making a strong effort to reduce the playtime of a single expedition in order to lessen the burden of repeated runs. We did consider simply reducing the number of battles or events in the existing expedition format, but we felt this would neither result in a satisfying gameplay experience nor necessarily make the game more enjoyable.

Instead, we decided to redesign the structure of this shorter expedition mode entirely. In the early stages, Tacticians will focus on building the team composition and setup, then take on a series of consecutive boss battles (with occasional events or encounters in between).

This Quick Expedition mode becomes available after you clear the game through Act 3 once. We are preparing it so that you can complete an expedition in over 50% less time compared to the existing format, and we hope this gives you a fresh way to enjoy the journey again.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/32c0928ae9173ecab6cef7cb27361c3aa84f16ce.png"]As multiple updates have made the game more accessible and easier to enjoy, we also found ourselves needing to reconsider how difficulty is handled. With Sable’s Wrath and Sable’s Whisper modes, Tacticians can already choose a difficulty that suits their preference, and Trials allow you to add conditions to make the game more challenging.

However, Trials do not simply make the game harder—they sometimes introduce difficulty modifiers that Tacticians may not necessarily want. Therefore, in this update, we are adding an option that allows you to separately adjust the mastery level of enemy units when selecting difficulty.

While we thought it would be ideal to allow adjustment of many different values, we determined that if we had to choose one factor that most meaningfully impacts difficulty, it would be the enemy mastery level.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/90c13ab6e7ff53c85c52eb0006408f6c8c7cf5b0.png"]There were many times when, after finishing an expedition, we felt that the build we had created was so satisfying that we wished to keep playing with it just a little longer.
Inspired by this idea, this update will introduce a feature that allows you to export the build from a completed expedition and replay certain combat scenarios using that build.

While preparing this build extraction feature, we also discussed various content ideas internally that could be built on top of this system. Unfortunately, we cannot include all of them at this time. Although there are no concrete plans yet for additional content, we hope that if you continue to enjoy and support the game, we may have opportunities to present more of these ideas in the future.
We hope you look forward to the February update, and we sincerely appreciate your continued support for Lost Eidolons: Veil of the Witch.
Jinsang Kim

items.text: Tacticians,
In our last dev log, we noted that we are working on a stronger roguelite experience and shorter expeditions. We have come up with many ideas, and are deploying some of them in our upcoming patch.
Based on feedback from players, the following are some of the boosts in the patch that will let you steamroll your enemies more easily!

Having the right relic at the right time can make a huge impact. So we added Blessed Relics that provide more powerful effects than their regular versions–and just in case it is not obvious… Some relics lose their penalty in their blessed version!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/5b4da8cdfaba95e8232ddb95712802bdaf276960.jpg"]\[Look at the holy halo behind those blessed relics!]

notes.title: We created 2 Talent skills for each character

items.text: Skill 1: Boosts each character's key attributes
Skill 2: Increases the proc chances for the character's Partnership effect
These new Talent skills are included as part of the skill card pool as Unique (purple) cards. Now you have even more skills to choose from!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/182cfe446f88f9f449e5cd8a093512997f2bab85.jpg"]\[Showing Evie's Talent Skill 2, which grants a much higher chance of triggering additional heals.]

Roguelites are often more fun with different unit comps and combos. The new Morale Boost system will make trying out different units even more enticing. Units who sit out on previous expeditions will have a chance to gain buffs–it is a 2-tiered buff with powerful effects. Experimenting with different characters has never been more rewarding!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/40ad8f61904497ebaa25153dea7bb6f5c7957db8.jpg"]\[Elena did not enjoy sitting out on action. Now she’s eager to show us what she can do!]
For a more streamlined experience, we adjusted the number of enemies and dialogue lines in some combat scenarios. This should let you jump in to action quicker!

On top of that, we reviewed 17 different Forked Road encounters to see how we can simplify things–many of them now have fewer dialogue lines and/or have choices consolidated. This would allow for both shorter events and more meaningful rewards with each choice.

The upcoming patch also contains other improvements and changes, so please stay tuned for the full patch notes coming soon! As noted at the top, there are also more ideas and content we are working on. You’ll have more to look forward to beyond this patch, and we cannot wait to bring more exciting news to you.

Hello, Tacticians!
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]We are updating Veil of the Witch to version 1.1.8 based on some of the feedback we've gotten after 1.0 release. Read on below for the details.
[p align="start"]
PT: November 3 4:30 PM
ET: November 3 7:30 PM
CET: November 4 1:30 AM
KST: November 4 9:30 AM
[p align="start"]
New Expedition Difficulty Options
Added difficulty selection, “Witch's Wrath” and “Witch’s Whisper.” Read more about this change HERE. This replaces the previous God Mode feature.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/ae3c87048f33e13a6c37c0cb9ee84b705d6151a3.png"]
Combat Difficulty Adjustments
The number of Vermiliths appearing in the Vermilith battle has been reduced, and other monster enemies now appear instead.
The failure condition for villager rescue maps has changed from “3 or more villagers killed” to “All allies defeated.” Successfully rescuing 3 villagers now grants additional rewards instead.
In the second Bernhardt battle, the damage reduction from his defense stance has been lowered from 90% to 50%.
In the third Bernhardt battle, Bernhardt’s HP recovery effect when receiving a critical hit now only activates while linked to his “Umbral Chains.”
Free Special Skin Set DLC - Rereleased for a Limited Time
For everyone who missed it the first time, Ashe's special skin set--including sword, bow, and armor--is now available again to download for free for one month.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/44d9db46f4b70a2c360cca9a66ba438d2bc51452.png"]
Relic Improvements
Cracked Wind-Up Soldier
Deals 15 damage to all enemies whenever an ally is defeated. Triggers up to 3 times per battle.
Scholar's Candelabrum
Speaking to an ally at camp raises their Physical/Magic Attack and Physical/Magic Defense by +3. This relic can be used 2 times, then no more.
Luminescent Box
At the start of the Ally Turn, any allies below half health regain 15 HP.
Bloody Effigy
For every status effect on an ally, they gain +3 Physical and Magic Attack, but -2 max HP.
Tattered Banner
Allies under 60% HP gain +10 to Physical and Magic Attack.
Notched Hilt
Upon acquiring, the max HP of all allies is reduced by 10. With each successive victory, max HP goes up by 5 (caps at +20).
Trap Skill Adjustments
Increased gold obtained from the “Pillaging Trap” effect.
Increased damage dealt by “Bomb Snare.”
Name and Text Updates
Added clarification that the “Phantom Grudge” area created by the “Dark Phantom” skill lasts for 5 turns.
“Melee Defense Stance” → “Riposte”
“Ranged Defense Stance” → “Repel”
System & Visual Improvements
When rerolling skills/stat cards, the card immediately before it will not appear again.
Added tutorials for certain enemy and elite enemy skills.
Added visual effects to help identify status effects.
New status effect visuals for Bernhardt’s “Riposte” and “Repel.”
Passive effect visuals for Fellheart’s “Shadow Armor” and “Shadow Shield.”
You can now find hints for recruiting new characters starting right after the prologue.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/3c581ae48f78e01e3c04dcb32adc14517d53a380.png"]
Achievement Adjustments
The cooperation stage requirements for the achievements, “Bury the Hatchet,” “Unspoken Feelings,” “A Better World,” and “Forgiveness Starts Within” have been reduced from 4 stages to 3 stages.
The event completion requirement for “Once Upon a Time” achievement has been reduced from 3 completions to 1.
If previously completed achievements were not properly recorded, they will now automatically unlock when the game starts.
Achievements earned during the demo will automatically unlock when starting the full version.
Fixed an issue where Vermilith would use Devour while under "Immobilized" status.
Fixed an issue in the third Fellheart battle where Fellheart only used "Shadow Cyclone" once.
Fixed a bug where Elena could make multiple moves under specific conditions while in “Lone Wolf” state.
Fixed an issue where when in Concealed state, counterattack damage did not show in preview.
Fixed an issue of “Lantern of the Dead” relic effect triggering when summons caused enemy retreats.

Fixed a progression blocker where, if “Raven Contract” and “Pumpkin Seed Bundle” relics were both owned, and “Pumpkin Seed Bundle” became disabled due to a crisis event, the player could no longer interact with the Raven thereby halting the expedition.
Fixed an issue where Behemoth would use the "Crashing Ram” skill on units in "Concealed" state.

We appreciate everyone that reported any bugs or issues that they came across during their gameplay. Please feel free to share your thoughts and suggestions with us on our Steam discussion boards or our Discord server.

items.text: Dear Tacticians,
We’re currently preparing the final release for Veil of the Witch, but we’re also working on an update to parts we hope to get more feedback about from Early Access players.
You heard that right: the official launch is just around the corner!

When we first entered Early Access, we mentioned that our goal was to release the full game within six months to a year. (Personally, I thought six months would be enough!) It’s taken a bit longer than expected, but we’ve since delivered according to our promised roadmap, and we look forward to sharing it all with you soon.
Here are the new things you can expect to see in the upcoming update…

notes.title: Balancing Boss Battles & Adding Act 3 Battles Variations

items.text: What did you think of the new boss fights in Act 1 and 2? It seems some players have found them quite challenging. While some of that difficulty comes from the novelty, there are parts that may genuinely be a bit too punishing.

So we’re making some adjustments to the new boss variants in Acts 1 and 2, to make them feel more manageable and clearly structured. And looking ahead, we’re also adding two new battle variations for the Act 3 boss fight. We’d love to hear your thoughts once they’re live!

We’re adding 9 new monster units, along with 8 new battle scenarios to go with them. These new encounters have been placed primarily in Act 1, giving players more variety in early-game maps, as Act 1 tends to be the most frequently played part of the game, so it can be the quickest to feel repetitive.
This update is built to address that. We’ve also adjusted some of the existing battles by changing their objectives. We look forward to your thoughts on the new battles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/2a6541eb4a1fab939cbb635bdb45383898f986ac.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/457712a7f6c8bcef980ddddace948e43f49b6092.png"]

Previously, the game had a system where your party couldn’t own multiple pieces of the same type of mythic equipment (for example, one-handed swords). Based on your feedback, we’ve changed that restriction.
We’re also introducing new, unique equipment skills, including 11 new active skills and 4 new passives. We believe this will make the gameplay experience feel a lot more dynamic and engaging!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/acfaafee2d0078ce5214e7880fed0b18fd53f38d.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/01cd503ff22a0a48ad94c8214b53c604ed5b96d6.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/9c0bdd369b7c2a0fb21b46e6b87679ce39d220da.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/fe9947db0445bfc0018253d77f46c177bfeb9297.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/5c27fa87e1953f336bccde09a54ff8be8ffe8a0a.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/1515094082e07807a40135902a60853e1d767034.png"]

During the Early Access period, we received a lot of feedback about the signposts players encounter while traveling. Once players have collected all the resources tied to a specific signpost, its value naturally decreases (although there are ways to exchange resources). In other cases, there are signposts that are rarely chosen based on the player’s preferred gameplay style.
Instead of forcing players to choose the less-desired signposts, we decided to encourage more diverse choices by offering more tempting incentives.

While playing, you may come across signposts that look a little unusual, like in the screenshot below. Try selecting one of them during your run and see what happens. We hope you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the effects!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44462767/9ad521c248d9bf3484b2e18b2031d334436a4b44.png"]
In addition to all the updates mentioned above, we’ve also added a bunch of new voiced lines to your party in combat, bringing the game to a more refined and complete state.
We can’t wait for you to jump in and try out all the changes!
Until next time,

Dear Tacticians,
Now, let’s dive into the new updates in this patch!
Among all the feedback we’ve gotten during Early Access, there are two key points we wanted to address immediately: replayability and repetitiveness.

Since this game incorporates roguelite elements, a certain amount of repetition is inevitable. However, some of that I felt was the perception of the experience of many battles being a little too similar. I was especially interested in feedback from players who have played the game for a fair amount of time—and wish to continue playing—but find that the game stops being as engaging after a certain amount of progress.
So let’s take a look at a few of the changes in this update (of which there are many) that should help to address the situation! There are three major features I want to highlight today.
Raven’s Tower, where you can craft Accessories and set your Trial level
Trials (18 Optional Effects and 7 Levels)
Various Trial effects can be combined together to increase the game’s overall difficulty.
As the difficulty increases, enemies become stronger, but you also gain access to unique reward currencies.
Originally, there were only three stages of trials. We felt that wasn’t enough, so now it goes up to seven.
Activating all 18 trial effects will make the game extremely, extremely difficult. I attempted it myself and didn’t last very long.
Accessories (19 Total)
As a reward for progressing while under the effects of a Trial, players can now craft Accessories that include new skills with new effects.
After it’s crafted, each accessory can also be upgraded one time.
Your party members can equip one accessory each.
Some accessories grant unique skills with a set number of uses.

Initially, these skills had really specific restrictions, like “only usable once every such-and-such number of battles”. But we decided that wasn’t very fun, so now they all just have a fixed number of uses in general, allowing for more strategic and flexible gameplay.
If used tactically, these Accessories can be game-changingly powerful.
Altar of Fire Upgrades (Further strengthening the effects of persistent upgrades)
To keep up with the added difficulty from Trials, we’ve added a new system to let players further enhance the upgrades available at the Altar of Fire.
All upgrades in the Altar of Fire can be enhanced with Sacred Embers.
After enhancing 30 upgrades, you’ll unlock the ability to slot one additional Greater Blessing.

Trials are a feature that allows players to adjust the game’s difficulty to their preference. We encourage you to experiment with various Trial effects to find the difficulty level that suits you best. And if you enable them all, be prepared for the ultimate challenge.

There’s a lot of ways to alleviate repetitiveness in a game like this, and some of them take a bit longer than others. In this update, we focused on adding more challenges and new abilities, woven into another track of persistent unlockables.

For the official release, we’ll be adding additional maps, more variations to battles, new enemies, another entire Act, and more. We've listened to our community’s feedback and adjusted our development plans accordingly. This new content will be designed to enhance replayability and keep the experience fresh for our players. We will share more in detail as we continue to develop new content! Stay tuned for more!
Best regards,
Jinsang Kim
